subject: botany
question_text: What are the first organisms to colonise rocks? Give the generic name of the moss which provides peat.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.7, VSAQ 5. The book's answer matches the NCERT sentence (mosses along with lichens; Sphagnum). Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Mosses along with lichens
lines: Mosses, along with lichens, are the first
steps.why: Bare rock has no soil. Lichens and mosses can still grow on it, and their growth and decay slowly build the first soil layer — so they begin plant succession on rocks.
common_mistakes: Naming only mosses or only lichens — the accepted answer names both together.
Writing 'fungi' or 'algae' — succession on bare rock starts with lichens and mosses.
steps.memory_tip: Rock succession starts small: a lichen crust first, a moss carpet with it, then larger plants.
steps.margin_note: One NCERT sentence answers the first part.

steps.label: Sphagnum — the peat moss

lines.text: Sphagnum — the moss that provides peat

lines: Dead Sphagnum accumulates in bogs and is
compressed into peat over many years.
steps.why: Sphagnum grows in wet bogs; its dead remains pile up and pack into peat. The question asks only for the generic (genus) name, so 'Sphagnum' is the answer.
common_mistakes: Writing 'Funaria' — Funaria is the common moss; Sphagnum is the peat moss.
Writing the genus without underlining it — a handwritten genus name should be underlined.
steps.memory_tip: Sphagnum and peat appear in one NCERT line — learn them as one pair: peat = Sphagnum.
steps.margin_note: The genus name alone earns the mark; underline it.

insider_note: This is two half-questions in one; a full answer names lichens together with mosses AND Sphagnum — students often stop after the first half.
